claims.text: BUDGET GUARD, INSTALLED ONCE, AT THE TOP. The fan-out scripts that night constructed the provider directly and never called daedalus.budget.install_process_guard, so ~170 paid calls left the machine unpriced before anyone noticed. The guard is not optional here and not a parameter -- a fan-out is exactly the shape that turns a missing guard into a bill.
claims.why: Reference to daedalus.budget.install_process_guard is not present in this chunk; no guard installation code is visible.

claims.text: CORROBORATION IS THE POINT, NOT A FEATURE. That night produced 1,226 claims whose largest agreement cluster was TWO, because the fan-out handed every agent a different file. N agents on N different things cannot corroborate anything; N agents on the SAME thing can. So votes is a first-class argument and every result records how many independent answers it is made of.
claims.why: FanoutTask has a 'votes' field (line 83) with docstring 'Independent answers to collect. >1 is what makes agreement meaningful.' This matches the claim that votes is a first-class argument.

claims.text: AND votes NEEDS temperature > 0, which is enforced rather than documented. The decode temperature defaulted to 0.0 and every caller inherited it. At 0.0 the decode is deterministic, so N samples of one prompt are IDENTICAL and three 'independent' votes are one answer counted three times -- which is indistinguishable from three agreeing agents in every downstream consumer. This paragraph used to be the only thing standing between a caller and fake agreement; fan_out now REFUSES the combination.
claims.why: The function fan_out is not defined in this chunk; no temperature enforcement is visible.

claims.text: A FRESH PROVIDER PER CALL. DeepSeekProvider.run resets self._written per call precisely so one instance cannot report a prior call's writes as this one's. Sharing an instance across worker threads would reintroduce that race by another door, so each call gets its own.
claims.why: No provider instantiation code present in this chunk; DeepSeekProvider is not imported or referenced.

claims.text: THE GRAPH GOES IN THE PROMPT. No provider module referenced structcore until 2026-07-30; the entire context a lane received was raw file bytes, and three of seven agent-written modules imported things that do not exist. Tasks that name paths get daedalus.lanes.graph_brief.render_brief prepended.
claims.why: render_brief is imported from .graph_brief (line 37), confirming it is used. No evidence of prepending in this chunk, but the import supports the claim.

claims.text: RESULTS ARE PUBLISHED, NOT WRITTEN. Via daedalus.atomic, so a reader tailing the output directory during a four-hour run never sees half a JSON document.
claims.why: write_text_atomic is imported from ..atomic (line 35), confirming atomic writes are used.

claims.text: Advisory only. There is no writable parameter and adding one would be a mistake: a write lane needs daedalus.lanes.checks.run_checks around every file and a rollback story per task, and a fan-out has neither. Volume and writes do not belong in the same primitive.
claims.why: No writable parameter visible; the function fan_out is not defined, so the claim about its absence cannot be verified.

claims.text: Concurrency ceiling. The lane is network-bound, so this is far above the core count -- but not unbounded: each worker holds a provider, a request and a response body, and the box also has to keep running whatever else is on it. MEASURED 2026-07-30: a hundred concurrent agents pushed the test suite past a 900 s timeout, and the gate read that timeout as failing tests. The suite is 4,146 tests and 765 s on this box when idle -- NOT the 105 s the handoff carried, which is a stale figure and the reason 18 minutes per gate mutation looked mysterious. If a measurement is running, pass a low number and mean it.
claims.why: DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY is defined as 8, which is a bounded number consistent with the claim that it is a ceiling.

claims.text: Per-call ceiling. Advisory calls that need longer than this are usually stuck.
claims.why: DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S is defined as 300, providing a timeout ceiling as claimed.

claims.text: Concurrency from the environment, or DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY.
claims.why: Function default_concurrency() reads DAEDALUS_FANOUT_CONCURRENCY env var and returns max(1, int(raw)) if set, else DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY.

claims.text: One question, asked votes times independently. key is the filename the answer lands under and the resume identity, so it must be stable across runs and safe as a path segment. It is derived from task_id rather than trusted, because a task id built from a commit message or a file path will contain separators.
claims.why: FanoutTask has fields task_id, objective, votes. The key property (line 90) is described as 'A filename-safe, collision-free, stable identity.' The docstring states it is derived from task_id; the code shows it is a property that presumably uses task_id. The exact derivation is not fully shown, but the claim is consistent with the partial code.

claims.text: The digest is appended rather than the sanitised name being trusted: a/b and a\b both sanitise to a_b, and two tasks sharing a result file would have one silently overwrite the other's answer. Dot runs are collapsed after sanitising.
claims.why: The key property implementation is truncated; the full logic is not visible in this chunk.
